year_display.en: Lecture to working men at Norwich, 1868
year_display.zh: 1868 年在诺里奇为工人所作的讲演

edition.en: Lay Sermons, Addresses and Reviews (London: Macmillan, 1870), as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 16729); the lecture complete, without Huxley's footnotes.
edition.zh: 据《俗人讲道、演说与评论集》（伦敦：麦克米伦，1870 年），以古腾堡计划电子书第 16729 号为底本；讲演全文，略去赫胥黎的脚注。

basis.en: Delivered in 1868 and published in 1868 and 1870; the author died in 1895.
basis.zh: 1868 年讲演，1868 年与 1870 年发表；作者卒于 1895 年。

note.en: Huxley gave this lecture to the working men of Norwich during a meeting of the British Association, holding up the chalk every carpenter keeps in his pocket. From it he reads, step by step and with evidence a listener could check, a seabed of microscopic shells, an ocean where England now stands, and a history of the earth told in rock. Notice the last paragraph: put the chalk into a hydrogen flame and it shines like the sun, which is what an hour of patient thought has done to it.
note.zh: 赫胥黎在英国科学促进会开会期间，给诺里奇的工人们作了这次讲演，手里举着每个木匠都揣在兜里的那种白垩。他从这一小块东西里，一步一步、用听众自己可以核对的证据，读出了一片由微小贝壳铺成的海底，一个曾经覆盖着今天英格兰的海洋，以及一部写在岩石里的地球历史。请留意最后一段：把白垩放进氢气的火焰里，它会像太阳一样发光——一个小时耐心的思考，对它做的正是这件事。

excerpt.orig: A great chapter of the history of the world is written in the chalk.
excerpt.en: A great chapter of the history of the world is written in the chalk.
excerpt.zh: 世界历史的伟大一章，就写在白垩里。
